chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), that he was asked:

about the man who buys a slave girl, so he has intercourse with her, then finds a defect in her after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not return her to her owner, but she is evaluated for the difference between the defect and her health, so it is returned to the buyer. Allah forbid that He make a wage for her.'

key_terms.فَيَقَعُ عَلَيْهَا: so he has intercourse with her (consummation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a buyer finds a defect in a slave girl after consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, the Imam clarifies that consummation does not invalidate the right to claim compensation for hidden defects (‘ayb), distinguishing this case from simple return. The buyer retains the slave but receives a monetary deduction equivalent to the value difference between a defect-free and a defective slave, ensuring fairness without the complexity of repudiation. This principle underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on precise valuation in commercial transactions involving human property.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having been asked

about the man who was sold the slave girl, so he fell upon her, then found a defect with her after that. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He cannot return her upon her (former) master, but she would be evaluated what is between the defective (one) and the correct (one), so it would be return upon the buyer. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forbid if he makes it to be a wage for her’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, was asked

about the case of a man who buys a slave-girl, then does sexual intercourse, then finds defect in her, and he (the Imam) said, ‘She cannot be returned to her owner, but she can be evaluated as perfect and defective, and the difference of the two prices is returned to the buyer, may Allah grant protection against designating it as her wages.’”
